A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–J. Full text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only on pages 1 and 15.

before.justification: v3 reports original numerical experiments on eigenproblems, parametric PDEs, iterative solvers and optimal control, together with Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including measured prediction errors, solver convergence, control outcomes and sensitivity results in Section 4 and Appendices E–J.

M1.justification: The subspace losses, larger-subspace prediction strategy and FFNO-based training and inference procedures are unchanged. Appendix B revises their theoretical justification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same quantum and elliptic eigenproblems, Burgers and elliptic PDEs, iterative-solver tasks, optimal-control problems and supplementary test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment, including interpolation and sign-adjusted regression, the POD and neural-operator baselines, kernel methods, and random or exact-subspace solver comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices F–J retain identical data splits, grids, subspace dimensions, hyperparameter searches, training budgets, evaluation metrics and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The loss and embedding comparisons, resolution-transfer tests, smoothness analyses, Jacobi damping case study, and split/hyperparameter sensitivity analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions already report five random train-test splits with means and standard deviations in Appendix J/Table 14. Best/worst grid-search summaries and other uncertainty reporting also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All experimental values, result entries, plotted curves, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–15 and Figures 1–11.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds explicit containment to Lemma 1 and repairs its existing proof: the SVD expression becomes UΣYᵀ, the modified first singular value becomes 0 instead of 1, the squared-norm decrement becomes σ₁² instead of σ₁, and Equation 21 uses cos² rather than sin² of principal angles. These are localized mathematical corrections within the retained construction; Theorem 2's statement and the other proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about subspace regression, embedding, theoretical justification, accuracy and applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning smoother learned mappings, numerical instability, Jacobi learning failures and inefficient learned bases are unchanged, as are the applicability qualifications and open representation-efficiency question.

D1.justification: Section 6 and the experimental appendices provide identical architecture, optimization, dataset-generation, training and code-access information.

R1.justification: The same 39 references and corresponding discussions are retained. Research positioning and relationships to earlier methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first author's affiliation changes from 'AXXX' to 'AXXX, AIC', the arXiv version/date stamp is updated, and limited wording changes accompany Lemma 1. The document's narrative and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 15 tables retain identical displays, captions and placement. Page organization and displayed-equation arrangements are also retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B removes several mathematical inconsistencies in the existing embedding proof, particularly the modified singular value and principal-angle identity. This improves the theoretical exposition, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged. The gain is limited: the proof still gives the squared derivative norm as tr(Σ), although Σ contains singular values, so the revision does not fully resolve its inconsistencies.
